correctness.rationale: Every pair of parallel lines covering a noncollinear triple is determined by a choice of paired points, hence at most three concepts; for a collinear triple all concepts have a common line and varying parallel mate, so the positive query class has dimension at most one. Three applications of the exact mistake-tree first-query recursion establish the upper bound four. Four collinear points and one transverse point allow all sixteen traces on three of the collinear points plus the transverse point when q>=4. At q=3, two-line concepts are complements of lines and the line family has exactly dimension two; at q=2 all concepts equal the whole plane. The independent finite-field enumerator reproduced all cases for orders 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11, including exact minimax and 16-trace checks. The proof does not infer universality from finite experiments.

value.rationale: This is a naturally defined geometric hypothesis class (exact unions of two distinct parallel affine lines), not an arbitrary finite slice: it answers the exact static and adaptive rank throughout the family of finite affine planes, including non-Desarguesian cases, isolates the first q=4 transition, and exhibits a useful three-positive-query localization method. It distinguishes the restricted double-line family from the unrestricted two-line VC-five phenomenon and general O(kd log k) closure bounds.
